native_result.query: In which years were individuals with a criminal record found to have significantly lower wealth compared to those without?
native_result.HypoA: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.
native_result.HypoB: Individuals with a criminal record (incarcerated 1985-1994) had significantly lower wealth than those without in ALL three years — 1985, 1990 and 1996 — with the gap widening over time (mean differences ≈ -$17.2k, -$57.6k and -$85.1k; median differences -$2,880, -$10,500 and -$8,500; all Welch p<1e-19, corroborated by Mann-Whitney and negative Hodges-Lehmann shifts with CIs excluding zero, and robust to dropping negatives and 1/99% winsorization). Because ever_jailed covers 1985-1994, the 1985 gap predates most incarceration and should be read as preexisting association/selection (those later incarcerated already had lower wealth), not as a causal effect of criminal records; the 1990 and especially 1996 gaps are consistent with incarceration additionally suppressing wealth accumulation. The association persists after adjusting for race and sex (HC1-robust OLS) and within males only. Limitations: nominal (undeflated) dollars, 1,899 fully duplicated rows kept (no ID), misspelled 'hipanic' race label left as-is, and zeros possibly masking missing wealth.
native_result.WorkflowB: Per-year (1985, 1990, 1996) available-case comparison of composite_wealth by ever_jailed in the NLSY79 processed dataset (12,013 rows; 289 jailed vs 11,724 not): descriptives per group/year; primary Welch t-test (alpha=0.05, two-sided) with Mann-Whitney U corroboration and Hodges-Lehmann shift + bootstrap CI as effect size; sensitivity analyses excluding negative wealth and winsorizing at 1/99%; secondary OLS wealth ~ ever_jailed + race + sex with HC1 robust SE, plus male-only (crude and adjusted) robustness. Criterion for 'significantly lower': Welch p<0.05 AND negative mean difference, same direction in Mann-Whitney/HL; ties would be decided by the robust median-based statistic (none occurred).

sub_hypo.text: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.
sub_hypo.context: Participants in the National Longitudinal Study of Youth's 1979 cohort, with wealth measured in 1985, 1990, and 1996.
sub_hypo.relations: Individuals ever jailed between 1985 and 1994 have significantly lower composite wealth in each of 1985, 1990, and 1996 than individuals not jailed during that period.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.

sub_hypo.text: Individuals incarcerated during 1985–1994 had significantly lower composite wealth in 1985 than those not incarcerated during that period. This gap reflects preexisting association or selection, rather than a causal effect of criminal records, because 1985 predates most incarceration.
sub_hypo.context: NLSY79 processed dataset (12,013 rows: 289 ever jailed and 11,724 not); available-case comparison for 1985.
sub_hypo.relations: Jailed-minus-not-jailed mean difference approximately −$17,200 and median difference −$2,880; Welch p<1e-19, corroborated by Mann-Whitney and a negative Hodges-Lehmann shift with a confidence interval excluding zero. Robust to excluding negative wealth and 1st/99th-percentile winsorization.

sub_hypo.text: Individuals incarcerated during 1985–1994 had significantly lower composite wealth in 1990 than those not incarcerated during that period.
sub_hypo.context: NLSY79 processed dataset; available-case comparison for 1990, within the 1985–1994 incarceration ascertainment period.
sub_hypo.relations: Jailed-minus-not-jailed mean difference approximately −$57,600 and median difference −$10,500; Welch p<1e-19, corroborated by Mann-Whitney and a negative Hodges-Lehmann shift with a confidence interval excluding zero. Robust to excluding negative wealth and 1st/99th-percentile winsorization.

sub_hypo.text: Individuals incarcerated during 1985–1994 had significantly lower composite wealth in 1996 than those not incarcerated during that period.
sub_hypo.context: NLSY79 processed dataset; available-case comparison for 1996, after the 1985–1994 incarceration ascertainment period.
sub_hypo.relations: Jailed-minus-not-jailed mean difference approximately −$85,100 and median difference −$8,500; Welch p<1e-19, corroborated by Mann-Whitney and a negative Hodges-Lehmann shift with a confidence interval excluding zero. Robust to excluding negative wealth and 1st/99th-percentile winsorization.

sub_hypo.text: The mean wealth disadvantage associated with incarceration widened from 1985 through 1990 to 1996. The 1990 and especially 1996 gaps are consistent with incarceration additionally suppressing wealth accumulation, but do not establish a causal effect.
sub_hypo.context: NLSY79 processed dataset; per-year available-case comparisons in nominal, undeflated dollars. The 1,899 fully duplicated rows were retained because no ID was available; zeros may mask missing wealth.
sub_hypo.relations: Mean differences became progressively more negative: approximately −$17,200, −$57,600, and −$85,100. Median differences were −$2,880, −$10,500, and −$8,500, so median gaps did not widen monotonically. The initial gap indicates preexisting association or selection.

sub_hypo.text: The negative association between incarceration during 1985–1994 and wealth in all three years persists after adjustment for race and sex.
sub_hypo.context: NLSY79 processed dataset; per-year OLS with HC1-robust standard errors. The misspelled race label 'hipanic' was retained unchanged.
sub_hypo.relations: In wealth ~ ever_jailed + race + sex models, incarceration remains negatively associated with wealth in 1985, 1990, and 1996.

sub_hypo.text: The negative association between incarceration during 1985–1994 and wealth in all three years also persists among males only.
sub_hypo.context: Male respondents in the NLSY79 processed dataset; crude and adjusted male-only robustness analyses.
sub_hypo.relations: Among males, incarceration remains negatively associated with wealth in 1985, 1990, and 1996 in crude and race-adjusted comparisons.
